About Aspora

People on the move deserve a bank that moves with them. Since 2022, Aspora has been building a borderless financial operating system that makes money as mobile and transparent as its users.

Backed by influential venture capitalists like Sequoia Capital, Greylock Partners, Hummingbird Ventures, Y Combinator & Global Founders Capital. We're a team of 150+ across India, the UK, the UAE, EU and the US, working with extreme ownership, radical candour, and an obsession with customer impact.

We celebrate builders who question assumptions, ship fast, and turn regulatory complexity into elegant solutions. If you’re driven to redefine what global banking can be, we’d love to build the future with you.

About the Role

People build lives across borders, and Aspora helps the Indian diaspora send money home and grow wealth in India. Growth here is won in a user’s first three months: a friend’s referral, a first transfer, a return next month. This role exists to turn that journey into a growth engine that compounds with every new cohort. You will own growth for our product, working closely with design, engineering, data and our CLM team.

You decide which bets to make, how big they should be, and when to stop one that isn’t working. What you build will shape how fast Aspora grows, and the growth playbook we take into every new market

Location

In Office || Bangalore

What You’ll Do

  • This is a role with full ownership of the journey at the heart of Aspora’s core business.

  • Diagnose where growth leaks. Go deep into funnels on every launch and older bet, and publish insights the whole team acts on.

  • Own the number and the path. Check the numbers daily, hold a clear view on opportunity areas, and open new growth threads.

  • Grow referral and activation. Ship reward constructs and product bets that bring more users in and get them to a first transfer.

  • Make new users stay. Lift retention in the first three months by turning a first transfer into a monthly habit.

  • Size every bet to matter. Set the payback before launch, read the result honestly, and call it early when a bet isn’t working.

  • Build trust after every transfer. Shape the post-transfer experience so customers feel informed and in control, even when timing slips.

What We’re Looking For

You’re not someone who measures a quarter by features shipped. You measure it by the number you moved, and you can show exactly how.

  • You’ve moved a growth number. You owned an acquisition, activation or retention metric in a consumer app and can walk through what moved it.

  • You live in the data. You write your own SQL or analytics queries and read an experiment properly: control groups, sample checks, significance.

  • You’ve run rewards with a payback. You designed referral, cashback or incentive programmes with the unit economics worked out before launch.

  • You ship experiments end to end. Hypothesis, launch, readout and the next iteration, more than once, on dates you agreed and kept.

  • You go to the source. You’ve turned user calls, session replays or research into a product decision that changed what shipped.

  • You know consumer products. You’ve built product or growth at a consumer app, and Indian consumer fintech experience is a strong plus.

  • You own the goal, not the task. You hold the number, the path to it and the next thread to pull, without waiting to be asked.

  • Most importantly, you want a number that is clearly yours, in a business where every cohort you keep compounds.

Why Aspora?

  • Own growth end to end, the core of Aspora’s business, with a number that is clearly yours.

  • Set the growth playbook Aspora carries into new markets and the products we build on top of remittance.

  • Full ownership from day one, not a slice of someone else’s roadmap.

  • Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and ESOPs aligned with Aspora’s long-term vision.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Consumer Bank Network team helps people do more with their bank accounts. We build consumer experiences for connecting financial accounts and making payments across Stripe, spanning Financial Connections and Link. We make these experiences simple, secure, and trustworthy.

The team owns the user experience for one of the highest-traffic products at Stripe. Our work spans onboarding, authentication, checkout, and returning user experiences. We combine product design, experimentation, and personalization to reduce friction, improve conversion, and help consumers discover and adopt payment methods that meet their needs. For businesses, this means easier customer onboarding and better payment experiences. This is both an application and platform team: in addition to the thousands of merchants integrating the Financial Connections UX, more than a dozen teams across Stripe also rely on Financial Connections to serve their users. 

Link is used by more than 300 million consumers. You’ll build consumer experiences within that ecosystem, where small improvements in conversion can help more people connect accounts, make purchases, and get paid.

What you’ll do

You’ll own the strategy and roadmap for consumer growth, conversion, and payment method adoption across Financial Connections and Link. You’ll work across the consumer journey, from connecting a financial account to completing a purchase, setting up a subscription, managing your finances with your agent of choice, or receiving a payout.

This role combines a high bar for consumer product craft with a disciplined approach to growth. You’ll turn user research and funnel analysis into ideas, work closely with Engineering, Design, and Data Science to test them, and scale what works. You’ll shape both the everyday details of the experience and larger changes to how people discover and use financial products.

Responsibilities

  • Set the product strategy and priorities for consumer conversion, growth, and payment method adoption across Financial Connections and Link.
  • Build a steady pipeline of experiments, from targeted UX improvements to new growth opportunities. Define hypotheses, success measures, and guardrails, then use results to decide what to ship, change, or stop.
  • Partner closely with Design and User Research to understand consumer behavior and create clear, intuitive experiences across consent, authentication, bank selection, and error recovery.
  • Partner with Engineering and Data Science to build personalized consumer experiences using machine learning and adaptive experimentation, improving conversion and payment method adoption while balancing user value, business outcomes, and consumer trust.
  • Own measurement of conversion, activation, and payment method adoption. Understand differences across consumer cohorts and use cases, and distinguish product impact from changes in traffic mix.
  • Work with Engineering to improve reliability and experience quality, resolve friction, and make it easier to deliver and evaluate product changes.
  • Lead work across Link, Payments, Financial Connections, and cross-functional teams such as Partnerships, Risk, and Legal. Address important merchant needs while keeping the team focused on its highest-impact opportunities.
  • Be the face of the product for Stripe’s users and external partners, showcasing and building demos and prototypes in collaboration with Engineering, Design, and Go-to-Market teams.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • A track record of growing consumer products, with direct ownership of measurable improvements in activation, conversion, adoption, or repeat use.
  • Experience leading an experimentation program, including forming hypotheses, interpreting results, and adapting your approach when the evidence challenges your assumptions.
  • Strong consumer product judgment and UX instincts. You work closely with designers, care about the details, and can make complex or unfamiliar tasks feel simple and trustworthy.
  • Strong analytical skills and a practical understanding of statistics. You can design and interpret experiments, reason about statistical power and confidence intervals, and use funnel and cohort analysis to make sound product decisions.
  • Experience partnering with engineers and data scientists on technically complex products, with the judgment to balance growth, quality, and implementation cost.
  • The autonomy and persistence to turn an ambiguous problem into shipped improvements, align teams around clear priorities, and communicate your reasoning in writing and conversation.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with payments, wallets, consumer fintech, marketplaces, or subscription products.
  • Experience with personalization, recommendation systems, or incentive programs, including evaluating their long-term impact and economics.
  • Experience building consumer and B2B2C products, where consumer needs, merchant requirements, and platform constraints all shape the user experience.

The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

2. Engineers and Product Teams They need low latency, production ready infrastructure. They use Allium to power wallets, trading systems, payment rails, staking infrastructure, and real time applications that cannot break.

3. Strategy, Research, and Executive Teams They need clarity and insight. They use Allium to understand ecosystem economics, market structure, user behavior, competitive dynamics, and where capital is flowing onchain.

And of course...agents 🦞. Our customers and users include Visa, Stripe, G-SIB Banks, Big 4 Accounting firms, BCG, Coinbase, Phantom, Uniswap and cited by the Federal Reserve.

About the role

We're hiring a Security Engineer to build and operate the controls that protect Allium's infrastructure, applications, employee systems, and use of AI. You'll work closely with Engineering and the person leading our security program to investigate threats, implement practical fixes, and automate security work.

As AI agents gain access to code, data, and tools, security needs to cover both human and machine activity. You'll help secure how agents operate while strengthening our defenses against automated attacks, credential theft, and compromised software dependencies. This is a hands-on engineering role: you'll write code, test controls, investigate real signals, and take findings through remediation.

What you'll do

  • Secure cloud infrastructure and access. Implement least privilege, phishing-resistant authentication, short-lived credentials, controlled privileged access, and reliable provisioning and deprovisioning. Improve cloud configuration, managed credential storage, and network protections with service owners. Improve secrets scanning and prevent credentials from entering source control.

  • Secure AI agents and developer tools. Help implement permissions, execution isolation, network restrictions, and audit trails for coding assistants, agents, and tool integrations, including MCP. Test how untrusted content could trigger prompt injection, tool misuse, or unintended data access, and build safeguards at the point where actions execute.

  • Build detection and response. Correlate identity, cloud, workload, and CI/CD telemetry to detect credential theft, unusual access, unauthorized agent actions, suspicious software changes, and data exfiltration. Investigate attacks across systems, reduce alert noise, and test response procedures with system owners, including session revocation, exposed-credential rotation, and removal of unauthorized access.

  • Reduce software supply-chain risk. Assess dependencies, CI/CD workflows, third-party integrations, and developer environments. Partner with engineers to validate findings, protect build and deployment credentials, and remediate vulnerabilities.

  • Move quickly on relevant threats. Maintain visibility into internet-facing services, including developer tools and management interfaces. Evaluate new vulnerabilities and active exploitation against our actual exposure. Help patch, isolate, revoke credentials, or apply compensating controls with service owners, then verify that the response worked.

  • Automate and document. Use code and APIs to improve access reviews, configuration checks, evidence collection, and remediation tracking. Use AI thoughtfully for security work, validating its output and protecting sensitive data.

  • Support employee security and enterprise assurance. Deploy, validate, and maintain endpoint protections and device security baselines, including prevention settings, tamper protection, encryption, and timely updates. Work with the owner of employee IT on identity and SaaS controls. Provide clear technical evidence for audits and customer reviews, and maintain useful runbooks.

What we're looking for

  • Typically 4+ years of relevant security, infrastructure, or software engineering experience, with direct responsibility for implementing security controls.

  • Hands-on experience with a major cloud platform and a strong foundation in identity, networking, operating systems, and access control.

  • Depth in at least two relevant areas, such as cloud security, detection and response, application security, vulnerability management, or corporate security.

  • Experience investigating technical problems from logs and system behavior, testing hypotheses, and following issues through to resolution.

  • Clear communication, practical judgment, and constructive working relationships with engineers and business teams.

Don't take our word for it, what our customers say about us (https://www.allium.so/blog#love)

What some cool people have to say about us:

  • The Information's Top 50 Startups (https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-to-the-informations-50-most-promising-startups-of-2025)

  • Mario Gabriele from The Generalist's Future 50 Startup List: https://www.allium.so/post/allium-named-awardee-of-the-generalists-inaugural-future-50-startups

  • Obsessiveness - The best people at Allium cannot put a problem down once they pick it up. We care more about the work than is strictly rational. Institutions trust us because our data is right. Right means caring about the small things. The decoded contract that ships with one wrong field. The label that is 99% accurate but wrong on the address that matters. The query that runs in 4 seconds when it should run in 400 milliseconds. Most companies tolerate these. We do not.

    Obsessiveness shows up as depth of care. It is not measured in hours worked or visible effort. You should feel something physical when work ships half-right. That instinct is what we hire for.

  • Pro Athlete Mindset - Consistency. Day in and day out, in pursuit of excellence. A win yesterday does not guarantee (or even imply!) a win tomorrow. I hope anyone who supports a failing sports team will feel the pain (cough Man United fans) of inconsistency

  • Figure It Out & Extreme Ownership - Every day is unexplored territory. There are new engineering frameworks, new legal docs, new compliance, new sales, new regulations, and new operational procedures every single day. If you don’t know it, learn it. If you can’t learn it, find someone or a product that does it. If you can’t find someone, find someone who can find someone. It is never a lack of resources, but lack of resourcefulness.

  • High Agency - (One of) the highest commonalities between all successful people is their responsiveness. Most successful billionaire CEOs still reply to emails within minutes (within working hours). And when you reply, respond fast with effective solutions - and even better, resolutions. If you’re looking for a superpower, you can’t go wrong with responsiveness. Well of course this doesn't make sense when you're an engineer coding in flow, but in general high agency of problem solving gets one very far in life

  • Leading from the Front - No one is going to listen (and adopt) your suggestion unless you lead by example. It’s one thing to say We need to do XYZ this better & it’s another thing to build an MVP and say “This is the way we should do things”. The proof of work and momentum goes a long way.

  • Strong Opinions On the Future (loosely held) - It is okay to be wrong, but what is not okay is not to have an idea of how a better future should be. Alliumites take pride in trying to improving everything about the company all the time.

  • Sense of (Allium) business smell - There are number of folks who live to eat at Allium, but the Allium smell we are talking about is that we love folks who naturally want to know why and how the work they are doing builds leverage for their teammates and also relates to the business goals

About the team

We invite people of all backgrounds (https://www.allium.so/about). We have engineers who learnt coding much later in life, who learnt coding on the side, we have engineers who are still in school and we also have engineers who went to the top schools (CMU, Stanford, UIUC, UPenn, Oxford, NUS, Cornell), all are welcome if one comes in with a curious mind and an infectious work ethic.

Administrative Benefits

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The Capacity & Efficiency Engineering team builds the software that manages, governs, and reduces Robinhood's AWS cloud spend across compute, databases, and storage, operating at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, data engineering, and FinOps. We own the full lifecycle of cloud cost, from attribution and forecasting to automation that rightsizes infrastructure at fleet scale and keeps a bursty, latency-sensitive trading platform both reliable and cost-effective. Our work carries CEO-level visibility, has already driven millions of dollars in annualized savings, and is delivered in close partnership with Infrastructure, Finance, and product engineering teams across Robinhood.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the team, you will own capacity and efficiency for Robinhood's storage and database fleet, from Aurora clusters to S3 and the caches and volumes in between. You will build the systems that size this fleet to demand: Aurora reader counts and writer sizes set from market hours, declared events, and live load instead of fixed schedules; databases, caches, and volumes rightsized to what they actually use; and S3 data kept in the right storage class, with lifecycle rules that keep growth in check. You will take each from recommendations the Storage team validates to automation that safely applies its own changes in production. This is a 0-to-1 build with measurable impact on reliability at market peaks and on the AWS bill.

This role is based in our Bellevue, WA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Build forecast-driven capacity planning for the storage and database fleet, turning traffic history, load tests, and known events (market open, earnings, IPOs, promotions) into plans that scale up ahead and back down after, with an expiry on every temporary capacity hold
  • Design and build a capacity planner for Aurora that sets reader counts and writer instance sizes from demand and load signals (IOPS, CPU, connections, replica lag), replacing fixed scaling schedules
  • Rightsize databases, caches, and block storage (RDS, ElastiCache, DynamoDB, EBS) on instance size, provisioned IOPS and throughput, and idle capacity, and keep them right-sized as load changes
  • Own S3 efficiency at scale: storage class and Intelligent-Tiering strategy, lifecycle and retention policies, noncurrent versions and incomplete uploads, and request costs, using Storage Lens and inventory data
  • Take every recommendation to closed-loop automation with guardrails, progressive rollout, and rollback, in partnership with the Storage infrastructure team, handling constraints such as AWS capacity shortages, fallback instance types, and connection pooling
  • Measure outcomes in cost and reliability (savings against baseline, forecast error, utilization, capacity left behind after events) and share our forecasts with the pod rightsizing system so compute and storage scale together

What you bring

  • Deep hands-on experience operating AWS storage and databases at scale, especially Aurora or RDS (MySQL or PostgreSQL) and S3, including replication, read scaling, storage classes, and lifecycle management
  • Capacity planning and forecasting experience: modeling time-series demand, load testing, and translating traffic into instance counts, sizes, and storage growth
  • A track record of rightsizing infrastructure from utilization data (CPU, memory, IOPS, throughput, bytes stored) without hurting latency or availability
  • Strong Python or Go engineering, with experience building automation that safely modifies production infrastructure (guardrails, progressive rollout, and rollback built in), not just systems that observe and report
  • Familiarity with AWS storage and database pricing (S3 storage classes and requests, Aurora I/O-Optimized vs. Standard, Reserved Instances) is a strong plus
  • Experience with bursty, event-driven workloads (trading, payments, ticketing) or with Spark, Airflow, or Kubernetes is a plus
